inspiration: Each zone area has two influence ids, one for the order side and one for the destruction side. An area only counts for a pin inside its explore region (AreaMapMgr.cs lines 79 and 89; Zone_Area.cs lines 51 and 54). Technique: a two-sided capture rule stored as zone data. Transferable as a tug-of-war capture meter per zone, drawn on the map and owned by the zone, not by a realm.

Hate is the attacker's share of all damage the creature has taken, and the target is the player with the highest share (CombatInterface.cs lines 29 to 36 and 355). Transferable to our hate list (engine-owned, MAX_ATTACKERS = 3). Defect to fix when adapting: the share depends on the total, so every hit changes everyone's number, and healing is not counted. Fix: add a short stickiness band and a healing term.

Leash: a creature more than a fixed distance from its spawn point evades (drops aggro on every attacker first, then stops combat) and walks home (CombatInterface.cs lines 271 and 298). Transferable to the leash in the fight loop (row 4). Keep the evade-clears-aggro step; change the instant drop to a short walk-back with a reset window.

The creature brain is a base class with separate passive, aggressive and guard brains (WorldServer/World/AI/, AgressiveBrain.cs line 10). Transferable as one brain base with data-selected brains per zone (row 2).
A global config flag can turn off realm-tagged PvP area rules for the whole server (ClientFileMgr.cs line 53). Transferable as one switch over zone rules, not per-zone code.
Terrain height can come from small bitmap maps sampled per pin, not from a mesh (ClientFileMgr.cs line 248). Idea for zone heightfields as a grey image per zone; cheap to author.

briefs.label: Two-sided capture meter
briefs.why: A zone capture that swings between two sides reads as a tug of war at a glance, and works on a small map.
briefs.keep: Two influence values per area; influence only counts inside the explore region.
briefs.change: Recreate as a clearly distinct original, never a copy: one meter owned by the zone, not by a realm; drawn as a ring with our own colours; contested zones flicker instead of changing colour.

briefs.label: Share-of-damage aggro
briefs.why: A share-based pick rule is simple and explains itself to players who ask why a monster switched.
briefs.keep: Hate equals the attacker's share of damage taken; highest share wins.
briefs.change: Recreate as a clearly distinct original: add a stickiness band so the target does not flip on small gaps; add a healing term; keep the hate list inside the engine as our rule requires.

briefs.label: Walk-home leash
briefs.why: A tether from spawn keeps fights in the zone; clearing aggro on leash stops endless chases.
briefs.keep: Distance-from-spawn tether; evade clears aggro on every attacker.
briefs.change: Recreate as a clearly distinct original: a slow walk-back with a short invulnerable reset instead of an instant drop; the tether radius comes from the zone data row.

briefs.label: Brain trio
briefs.why: Three behaviour classes (passive, aggressive, guard) behind one base keep creature AI easy to read and extend.
briefs.keep: One base brain class; passive, aggressive and guard variants.
briefs.change: Recreate as a clearly distinct original: brains chosen per zone catalogue row, plus a fourth brain that patrols a route; our naming and states.
